diagram_math_checks.evidence: Input (line 40) fixes ordered n-qubit address and m-qubit target registers. Top |0^n> and bottom |0^m> therefore represent C^(2^n) and C^(2^m), with address first, as in def-qa-standard-bit-query Definition. New prose explicitly says these are entire register lines. The allowed m=0 occurs only at n=1 and gives the single empty-word basis state and a sole measurement outcome.

Definition instruction 1 (line 44) applies H tensor n to the address alone and leaves the target zero. The first top-only H box is before U_f. Instruction 3 (line 46) applies another H tensor n to that same address after target measurement; its box is drawn strictly to the right of target M_Z. Each H box denotes n exact one-qubit gates per lem-qa-hadamard-f2-kernel Statement and Facts F2–F5.

The single U_f rectangle spans both register lines and is neither a controlled-query symbol nor an inverse query. The formula below repeats exactly instruction 2 and def-qa-standard-bit-query: |x>|z> maps to |x>|z XOR f(x)>. It preserves address width n and target width m, with one query. Two H tensor n boxes give 2n Hadamards, matching line 48.

Bottom M_Z is defined in the new prose as the instruction-2 computational measurement with branch P_v X P_v, P_v=I_address tensor |v><v|, so its outcome v has m bits. The arrow ends at v: discard and has no connection to the address. Top M_Z follows the second Hadamard and returns n-bit y, matching instruction 3. No postselection or failure branch is asserted.

The original algorithm explicitly delegates the sample law to thm-qa-simon-hadamard-sampling-law. Its Facts F1–F5 and Proof steps 1.1–4.1 use the coset state, tensor-Hadamard amplitudes and Born rule; none uses a figure. The new schematic asserts only the existing operational order and gate count, and the final prose explicitly retains proof independence.
